feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Self-Supervised Visual On-Policy Distillation (S^2VOPD) creates an informative teacher-student asymmetry without privileged labels or stronger models by distilling an unaugmented visual distribution into a strongly augmented student view.

Why it matters: It enables state-of-the-art visual reasoning capabilities in smaller vision-language models without requiring ground-truth annotations, human reward signals, or larger teacher models.

entry.title: VibeWorlding: Can Multimodal Agents Construct 3D Open Worlds End-to-End?
entry.summary:
VibeWorlding introduces a framework, benchmark, sandbox environment, and multimodal RL-trained models to evaluate and improve end-to-end 3D open world construction by multimodal agents.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that targeted reinforcement learning post-training can allow open-source MLLMs to outperform leading proprietary models in complex 3D tool use and spatial world generation.

entry.title: HarnessEval-W: Agentifying the Evaluation of Visual Worlds
entry.summary:
HarnessEval-W is an agentified evaluation pipeline for visual world models that replaces scalar metrics with a transparent, verifiable evidence tree generated by specialized sub-agents.

Why it matters: It replaces opaque, brute-force scalar metrics with interpretable and verifiable reasoning chains to accurately assess physics and causality in world model rollouts.

entry.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness
entry.summary:
ClawGym II introduces a unified black-box RL framework using sandbox execution infrastructure and proxy-intercepted trajectory prefix trees to train agents like Qwen3-30A3B through complex, heterogeneous harnesses.

Why it matters: It enables stable, scalable reinforcement learning for LLM agents operating within complex, black-box execution harnesses on long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
entry.summary:
SimpleOPD enables tokenizer-agnostic on-policy distillation from long-context teacher models to short-context students using shared text-space token alignment and constrained reference KL loss.

Why it matters: It allows smaller, short-context open-weights models to efficiently acquire advanced long-form reasoning capabilities from specialized teachers without requiring identical tokenizers.

entry.title: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
entry.summary:
UI-Mate is an open-weight 27B GUI foundation agent trained with an environment-grounded stack and in-context demonstration learning, setting new open-weight state-of-the-art performance on OSWorld-Verified and WindowsAgentArena.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that combining in-context multimodal demonstrations with online RL substantially improves the execution reliability of open-weight models during long-horizon desktop automation tasks.

entry.title: DFM Mimir v1: An Open HRM Delivering Frontier Performance at 1B Parameters Using Only Permissible Post-Training Data
entry.summary:
Mimir v1 is an open 1-billion-parameter Hierarchical Reasoning Model trained from scratch using only permissible post-training data across 161 datasets.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive frontier performance in smaller language models can be achieved using strictly ethically sourced and permissible datasets.

entry.title: Agentic Transaction: Towards ACID-Compliant Agent Systems
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the concept of agentic transactions, framing LLM agent execution around an ACID-compliant framework featuring four semantic guarantees to improve reliability in dynamic workflows.

Why it matters: Adapting database transactional guarantees to agent architectures provides a principled mechanism for reliable, safe, and durable long-horizon task execution.

entry.title: GenRouter: Unified Workflow Routing for Agentic Image Generation
entry.summary:
GenRouter is the first unified workflow routing framework for agentic image generation, dynamically routing prompts to optimal workflow topologies to improve visual alignment while cutting compute costs by over 95%.

Why it matters: It prevents compute-mismatch in agentic image generation by dynamically matching prompt complexity to the necessary workflow, drastically reducing operational latency and cost.

entry.title: An Empirical Study of Training Pixel-Space Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
Researchers established a latent-to-pixel training strategy that overcomes slow pixel-space pre-training, enabling pixel-space text-to-image diffusion models to match or exceed latent-space performance while achieving up to 4.75x inference speedups.

Why it matters: This recipe eliminates the efficiency trade-off of pixel-space diffusion models, delivering significantly faster end-to-end image generation without compromising output quality.

entry.title: MegaParts: Scaling Part-Aware 3D Object Generation to 300 Parts via Token-Efficient Autoregressive Modeling
entry.summary:
MegaParts is an autoregressive 3D generation framework using a token-efficient vector-quantized shape tokenizer to scale part-aware generation up to 300 parts and 256k-token sequence lengths.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that token-efficient autoregressive modeling can replace diffusion models for high-fidelity 3D object generation requiring complex, fine-grained part assemblies.

entry.title: Understanding Cognition-Induced Risks in Agentic AI Systems
entry.summary:
A new framework categorizes cognition-induced risks in LLM-powered agentic AI systems across physical, social, and self-referential levels to analyze threats to human agency, autonomy, and control.

Why it matters: Systematically categorizing how expanding AI cognitive capabilities threaten human control provides a structured foundation for designing actionable safety guardrails in autonomous agentic systems.

entry.title: R^3-Bench: LLMs Struggle with Resource-Rational Reasoning under Shared Budgets
entry.summary:
R^3-Bench introduces a benchmark to evaluate LLMs on resource-rational reasoning under shared computational budgets across math, programming, and abstract reasoning in tool-free and agentic environments.

Why it matters: Current LLMs suffer from a gap between their baseline problem-solving competence and their ability to dynamically allocate compute under global budget constraints.

entry.title: Ventor-QTest: Threat-Model-Driven Verification of Vendor-Hosted LLM APIs
entry.summary:
Ventor-QTest is a black-box audit tool that evaluates vendor-hosted LLM API fidelity using repeated requests and long-sequence probes without requiring logprob access.

Why it matters: It enables model consumers to audit third-party API quality and detect silent performance degradation in long-horizon agentic workflows without relying on vendor-provided log probabilities.

entry.title: VideoGAIA: A Benchmark for General AI Assistants on Agentic Video Understanding
entry.summary:
VideoGAIA is a new benchmark featuring 271 model-human co-designed tasks that evaluates multimodal models on multi-turn, tool-augmented agentic video understanding.

Why it matters: It establishes a harder, tool-use-focused benchmark to drive the evolution of multimodal LLMs from static video question answering to dynamic, agentic interaction.

entry.title: Would this change your answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior In The Wild with Counterfactual Experiments
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that discovers naturally-occurring LLM behaviors and generates explanations evaluated through counterfactual prompt edits.

Why it matters: CHIVE provides an automated framework to rigorously evaluate interpretability techniques and produce training data that improves counterfactual reasoning about LLM behavior.

entry.title: Le Critique: Privileged Value Functions for LLM Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Le Critique introduces Privileged Value Functions (PVF) and the TETHER baseline to enhance token-level credit assignment and performance in LLM reinforcement learning over standard value functions and GRPO.

Why it matters: The approach makes learned value functions more practical and performant for LLM training, offering fine-grained token-level credit assignment without relying on large rollout groups.

entry.title: Does the LM Head Create a Harmful Gradient Bottleneck? A Causal Test
entry.summary:
A backward-only intervention study isolates LM-head gradient rank reduction, showing that while gradient compression exists, it is far less harmful than forward-pass factorized projections and does not constitute a primary optimization bottleneck.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that geometric compression in the LM head does not severely bottleneck optimization, indicating that architectural modifications targeting gradient rank projection yield minimal optimization benefits.

entry.title: HalluTracer: Hallucination Detection via Depth-Averaging Truth Signals
entry.summary:
HalluTracer is a white-box detection framework that aggregates weakly correlated truthfulness signals across all network layers during the forward pass using depth averaging to reduce noise.

Why it matters: By capturing truthfulness signals distributed across the entire model depth rather than relying on single-layer probes, developers can build more reliable hallucination detectors for high-stakes LLM deployments.

entry.title: Step-Level On-Policy Distillation: Interpolating Between On-Policy Distillation and Supervised Fine-Tuning
entry.summary:
Step-Level On-Policy Distillation (SOPD) provides step-level teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories to interpolate between the long-horizon corrections of SFT and the state-alignment advantages of OPD.

Why it matters: SOPD provides a superior distillation framework for reasoning and agent tasks by combining long-horizon path corrections with on-policy state alignment.

entry.title: Prior Audit-Repair Context Shifts LLM Verifier Thresholds Toward Leniency
entry.summary:
Including a completed audit-repair episode in an LLM verifier's context systematically shifts its decision threshold toward leniency, reducing false alarm rates on subsequent tasks by 2.8 to 11.5 percentage points.

Why it matters: Wiring LLM checkers and fixers sequentially alters the checker's baseline severity threshold, meaning verifier accuracy and strictness depend heavily on prior in-context interaction history.

entry.title: From Sequence to Structure: Relational Uncertainty Propagation for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
RUPA is a trajectory-level uncertainty quantification framework for LLM agents that models execution histories as directed dependency graphs to propagate risk across long-range reasoning steps, tool interactions, and environment feedback.

Why it matters: By accounting for long-range dependency chains rather than isolated step probabilities, RUPA enables earlier detection of agent failures and improves execution reliability in complex, long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Aborted but Not Forgotten: KV-Cache Retention Breaks Rollback Consistency in Language Agents
entry.summary:
Researchers identify a state integrity failure where language agents retaining KV-cache state attend to logically aborted transcript branches, breaking rollback consistency even when the served prompt text is clean.

Why it matters: Applications relying on agentic rollback or time-travel mechanisms remain vulnerable to prompt injection or state corruption unless the underlying KV-cache is explicitly restored alongside the text transcript.

entry.title: Towards Computational Provenance: Carrying Causal-State Evidence in Generated Text
entry.summary:
A controlled study demonstrates that neural models can embed detectable, verified causal-state evidence into subtle statistical patterns of generated text without altering the final output answer.

Why it matters: It provides a proof of concept for establishing computational provenance, enabling third parties to verify which internal neural pathways were executed to produce a model's output.

entry.title: What Do Compliance Detectors Read? An Audit of Activation Probes and Guard Models
entry.summary:
Researchers identify "rule blindness" in compliance detectors and activation probes, showing their verdicts rely on scenario surface features rather than governing rules, and propose the training-free Internal Compliance Score (ICS) for efficient auditing.

Why it matters: Deployed AI compliance guards may offer a false sense of security by triggering on scenario context rather than actual regulatory rule violations.

entry.title: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? A Systematic Evaluation of Detectors, Generators and Social Dissemination
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced RA-Bench, a benchmark of 17,886 videos across 10 social-risk categories, revealing that current AI video detectors fail to generalize and degrade further during social dissemination.

Why it matters: Existing deepfake detection pipelines are unreliable for real-world crisis management because they fail to generalize to modern video generators and degrade under social media sharing conditions.

entry.title: Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development
entry.summary:
A new evaluation framework uses rule-based metrics and controlled comparisons across 36 long-horizon tasks to analyze seven frontier agents' internal behaviors, experience reuse, and execution bottlenecks beyond final scores.

Why it matters: Evaluating internal agent behaviors and experience reuse rather than relying on static end-state scores provides actionable insights for improving LLM training, inference-time strategies, and harness design.

entry.title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning
entry.summary:
Intern-S2-Mobius introduces Mobius-v0, an architecture that decouples knowledge storage from reasoning by utilizing a globally shared feed-forward network memory and multiple self-attention reasoners.

Why it matters: Decoupling knowledge from reasoning significantly reduces training data requirements and dramatically improves model inference efficiency without sacrificing downstream task performance.

entry.title: MobileMem: Learning from a Year of Mobile Experiences
entry.summary:
MobileMem is a new benchmark and framework for on-device long-term memory, built on a year-scale collection of mobile experiences to evaluate continuous, multimodal agent learning.

Why it matters: It enables the evaluation and development of persistent personal AI assistants that can adapt to changing user preferences and context over long periods on mobile devices.

entry.title: HumanTracker: Towards Comprehensive and Human-Aligned Motion Tracking Benchmark
entry.summary:
HumanTracker is a humanoid motion tracking benchmark providing 153 hours of optical motion trajectories and HumanScore, a preference-aligned metric trained on 12K motion pairs to detect stability and contact failures.

Why it matters: It enables more accurate evaluation of humanoid tracking algorithms by capturing contact-rich, long-horizon physical instabilities that standard kinematic metrics overlook.

entry.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing
entry.summary:
CPI-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating real-world image editing models across multi-image inputs, practical user scenarios, and complex reasoning-based instructions.

Why it matters: CPI-Bench provides a human-aligned, reliable standard to quantify model gaps in real-world deployment and complex multi-image reasoning tasks.

entry.title: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
entry.summary:
Claim-Level Reliability Assessment (CLR) is a training-free framework that improves test-time reasoning by decomposing traces into critical claims and using semantic falsification to target errors.

Why it matters: It enables large language models to achieve higher reasoning accuracy with reduced token consumption during test-time compute allocation.

entry.title: Forecast Collapse in Time-Series Foundation Models
entry.summary:
Researchers identified forecast collapse in time-series foundation models on low-predictability targets and introduced CalibRank, an objective function that balances forecast calibration and cross-sectional ranking accuracy.

Why it matters: Standard per-series evaluation metrics obscure cross-series structural failures, which can render foundation model forecasts unusable for downstream multi-asset decision-making.

entry.title: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5: A Toolkit for Robot Process Assessment
entry.summary:
PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5 is a robot process assessment toolkit that converts rollout videos into dense progress curves to measure failure-side progress, post-drawdown recovery, and execution quality beyond binary success rates.

Why it matters: It enables fine-grained, transparent, and reproducible evaluation of embodied AI models beyond simple binary success metrics.

entry.title: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance
entry.summary:
Marionette introduces a game world model that decouples dynamics from rendering by predicting explicit 3D world states, converting them to pose-control videos via a zero-parameter graphics engine, and synthesizing RGB frames using a video-diffusion model.

Why it matters: Decoupling explicit world-state dynamics from appearance rendering eliminates compound error accumulation in long-horizon game simulations and allows direct programmatic control over physics and character interactions.

entry.title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation (LOPD) makes the teacher's privileged context learnable end-to-end via continuous latent tokens rather than relying on designer-specified artifacts like answers, skills, or feedback.

Why it matters: By eliminating human-engineered privileged context, LOPD enables more scalable, sample-efficient, and end-to-end self-improvement for autonomous agents.

entry.title: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel as LLM Agents Act and Observe
entry.summary:
Second Thought is a training-free inference framework that runs parallel auxiliary reasoning branches during the action-observation idle window of LLM agents to reduce main-thread sequential decoding without sacrificing task accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables LLM agents to perform deeper reasoning without increasing main-thread latency, accelerating agent execution times while maintaining or improving benchmark success rates.

entry.title: Scaling Domain Data Repetition in LLM Pretraining
entry.summary:
A study on scaling domain data repetition shows that optimal repetition counts mildly increase with model size at a fixed tokens-per-parameter ratio and correlate negatively with a domain's final validation loss.

Why it matters: Practitioners can safely reuse high-quality data repetition schedules optimized on smaller proxy models to prevent domain dilution in larger models without causing severe overfitting.

entry.title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced LITTLECURRICULUM, an 88B-token elementary-level corpus, and LITTLELEARNER, a 5B-parameter model trained on it to establish controlled, interpretable knowledge boundaries for studying LLM capability acquisition.

Why it matters: This controlled sandbox allows researchers to study how language models acquire, represent, and use knowledge without the confounding effects of heterogeneous, web-scale pretraining data.

entry.title: UniProbe: A Learnable Token-Level Hallucination Detector for Large VLMs using Multi-Structural Internal Representations
entry.summary:
UniProbe is a learnable token-level hallucination detector that models a frozen LVLM's computational trace using interleaved GNN, ViT, and GRU modules over a directed graph of attention weights.

Why it matters: It enables real-time, low-latency mitigation of vision-language hallucinations at the token level without requiring computationally expensive full-model retraining or external verifiers.

entry.title: Handover of In-Context Learning State Across Session Boundaries
entry.summary:
This study establishes a theoretical framework for session handover in large language models by framing context transfer as preserving task-relative in-context learning states under strict memory constraints.

Why it matters: It provides a mathematically grounded methodology for determining exactly what context to compress or retain when switching sessions, agents, or memory windows without sacrificing downstream predictive performance.

entry.title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
entry.summary:
SimpleOPD enables tokenizer-agnostic on-policy distillation from long-context teacher models to short-context students by aligning text-span tokens and using constrained KL loss to stabilize generation length.

Why it matters: It enables smaller, short-context models to efficiently absorb advanced proof-reasoning capabilities from long-context teacher models without requiring identical tokenizers or risking training instability.

entry.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters
entry.summary:
sMuon adapts the Muon optimizer for low-rank fine-tuning by approximating a relaxed objective through linearization and least-squares, enabling low-rank updates using only matrix multiplication operations.

Why it matters: It enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA to leverage the optimization benefits of Muon using computationally efficient matrix multiplications.

entry.title: Designing Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: A Unified Path-Space View
entry.summary:
This paper unifies reverse-trajectory and forward-matching diffusion RL methods under a single path-space policy-gradient framework, revealing that empirical performance gaps stem from variance reduction rather than differing algorithmic principles.

Why it matters: It clarifies the mathematical connection between fragmented diffusion-RL algorithms, allowing practitioners to systematically design more stable, variance-reduced post-training recipes for image diffusion models.

entry.title: More Correct Mass, Worse Answers: Why Power Sampling Can Fail and How to Fix It
entry.summary:
Researchers identified critical mismatches in inference-time Power Sampling that degrade downstream performance and proposed a deformation-controlled, support-preserving target to fix them.

Why it matters: Fixing Power Sampling enables verifier-free inference-time reasoning techniques to improve accuracy without accidentally destroying the trajectory diversity needed for search and aggregation.

entry.title: Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations
entry.summary:
Researchers identified two scale-dependent intrinsic dimensionality (ID) regimes in language model representations driven by dataset lexical diversity and derived an exact, parameter-free formula predicting the exact reversal point between them.

Why it matters: Practitioners cannot treat intrinsic dimensionality as a simple proxy for representation complexity without accounting for dataset lexical diversity and scale dependencies.

entry.title: Amplified Does Not Mean Predictive: Reasoning Behaviors in Thinking Models
entry.summary:
A study introducing Behavioral Lift across 15 models and 15,282 traces reveals an Amplification-Lift Gap, where reasoning-oriented training amplifies behaviors like uncertainty acknowledgment without increasing high-correctness behaviors like confidence calibration.

Why it matters: Reasoning training optimizes surface-level deliberative traces rather than predictive correctness, highlighting the need for process-level objectives that reward grounded and calibrated reasoning.

entry.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation
entry.summary:
A framework that separates LLM evidence interpretation from decision aggregation using a four-field evidence tuple, correcting count-scale drift by pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios instead of raw score summation.

Why it matters: Fixing the arithmetic of multi-source evidence aggregation prevents systematic calibration drift without requiring larger language models or complex architectural changes.

entry.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin
entry.summary:
Twin uses a frontier coding agent to generate and iteratively repair executable world models at test-time for zero-shot grid games, achieving a 93.3% score on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark.

Why it matters: This approach demonstrates that frontier LLMs can automatically reverse-engineer executable environment dynamics and unseen goals purely through test-time interaction and code refinement.

entry.title: Knowing When to Stop: Bayesian Optimal Stopping for LLM Evaluations
entry.summary:
The optstop framework uses precision-based Bayesian adaptive stopping to dynamically allocate LLM evaluation compute based on uncertainty rather than fixed sampling budgets.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces compute costs and runtime for LLM benchmarking without sacrificing statistical confidence or accuracy in the final results.

entry.title: From Inaudible Inputs to Model Failures: Low-Frequency Safety Risks in LALMs
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Intermittent Low-Frequency Lockout (ILL), an inaudible black-box attack using low-frequency signals to degrade Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs), and proposed Distributional Requery Guard (DRG) to mitigate it.

Why it matters: It identifies a critical safety vulnerability where inaudible, low-frequency audio signals can severely disrupt LALM performance without alerting human users.

entry.title: CW-BASS v2: Saturation-Aware Pseudo-Label Selection for Semi-Supervised Segmentation under Foundation-Model Teachers
entry.summary:
CW-BASS v2 is a saturation-aware pseudo-label selection method for semi-supervised segmentation that dynamically switches between strict confidence filtering and an adaptive floor based on teacher reliability measured on a held-out slice.

Why it matters: It prevents pseudo-label filtering failures when using modern self-supervised foundation models as teachers, automatically adapting the filtering strategy without manual tuning across diverse benchmarks.

entry.title: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement
entry.summary:
TailBooster is a model-agnostic, dual-layer generative framework that uses statistical tail extraction and deep learning anomaly filtering to generate operationally valid tabular synthetic data for extreme events.

Why it matters: It enables accurate prediction of rare, high-impact disruptions without needing hardcoded domain-specific rules or sacrificing operational data validity.

entry.title: PixSDS: Why Latent SDS Makes Noisy Pixels
entry.summary:
PixSDS resolves VAE-induced pixel drift and high-frequency noise in latent Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) by using decoded lookahead steps to guide pixel-space gradients without changing the underlying diffusion model or SDS objective.

Why it matters: It fixes visual artifacts and high-frequency noise in text-to-3D generation workflows using a lightweight, plug-and-play gradient correction method.

entry.title: Toward a Gricean Retreat: Probing LLMs for Knowledge Boundaries and Referent Specificity
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that while LLM internal activations contain signals for both knowledge boundary awareness and upcoming referent specificity, current generation policies fail to reconcile them to perform a Gricean retreat to safer, generic claims.

Why it matters: Identifying that knowledge awareness exists in model representations provides a foundation for developing steering or alignment objectives that reduce hallucinations by forcing models to fall back to generic, true statements.

entry.title: Synthetic Persona Pretraining: Alignment from Token Zero
entry.summary:
Synthetic Persona Pretraining (SPP) embeds value-aligned assistant personas from the start of pretraining using normative reflection annotations, improving model alignment and jailbreak robustness after post-training persona binding.

Why it matters: Pretraining-time persona interventions prevent values from acting as a superficial overlay, producing AI models that are inherently resilient to misalignment and jailbreaks without degrading core capabilities.

entry.title: A Unifying Perspective on Causal World Models: From Observations to Representations to Structure
entry.summary:
This paper provides a formal definition of Causal World Models (CWMs) that unifies observational generation, object-centric representations, structural dynamics, and formal identifiability guarantees for causal reasoning and decision-making.

Why it matters: Grounding world models in formal causal representations enables AI agents to reliably predict, plan, and generalize beyond their training distributions.

entry.title: Are You Sure You're Sure? On the Impact of Instruction Tuning on Confidence and Lexical Diversity
entry.summary:
Instruction tuning alters LLM confidence and reduces cross-rationale diversity without significantly improving predictive accuracy, demonstrating that verbalized confidence and rationale diversity capture distinct, persistent effects.

Why it matters: Instruction tuning can induce model overconfidence and narrower rationale generation without delivering proportional gains in answer accuracy, complicating reliability in question-answering applications.

entry.title: It's How You Ask: Gender-Associated Linguistic Bias in LLMs
entry.summary:
A study reveals LLMs systematically generate shorter, less sophisticated, and less formal responses when prompts use female-associated linguistic features, regardless of explicit gender names.

Why it matters: Linguistic bias in LLMs can create disparate impacts in professional workplaces by penalizing communication styles commonly used by women.

entry.title: TsuGO: Probing Search Efficiency in LLM Reasoning via Go Life-and-Death Problems
entry.summary:
TsuGO is a new benchmark that uses Go life-and-death problems to evaluate LLM search efficiency by parsing chain-of-thought outputs into structured search trees.

Why it matters: It establishes search organization and resource allocation as critical, measurable dimensions in LLM reasoning beyond simple final-answer accuracy or CoT token length.

entry.title: GEM: A Generative Embedding Model Bridging Reasoning and Retrieval
entry.summary:
GEM is a generative embedding model that unifies reasoning and retrieval by generating context about query intent and appending an embedding token to represent the enriched context for vector search.

Why it matters: GEM closes the semantic gap between complex user reasoning instructions and traditional dense retrieval models without relying on separate multi-stage pipelines or larger external models.

entry.title: SkillShapley: Boundary-Adaptive Shapley Valuation for Skill Step Attribution in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
SkillShapley is a two-phase framework that uses boundary-adaptive Shapley valuation to estimate the performance contribution of individual steps within LLM agent skills.

Why it matters: It enables developers to automatically identify and refine high- or low-value steps in long procedural agent skills without relying solely on manual evaluation.

entry.title: Intern-S2-Preview: Scientific Agentic Foundation Model
entry.summary:
Intern-S2-Preview is a scientific agentic foundation model series featuring a 397B backbone and unified post-training, optimized for multimodal scientific reasoning, time-series forecasting, and long-horizon agentic tasks.

Why it matters: It enables scalable scientific discovery by combining long-horizon tool interaction, specialized memory extensions, and multimodal time-series forecasting without retraining massive base models.

entry.title: Neural Quadratic Forms: A Unified Minimal Model for Sudden Learning and Scaling Laws
entry.summary:
A unified mathematical model using symmetry-derived quadratic forms reduces various neural architectures to Lotka-Volterra dynamics, explaining both abrupt step-like learning and smooth power-law scaling during training.

Why it matters: It offers a single theoretical foundation to predict, compute, and analyze both sudden phase transitions and power-law scaling dynamics across diverse deep learning architectures.

entry.title: A Probe Direction Is a Property of Its Prompt
entry.summary:
Published probe scores for detecting evaluation awareness reflect arbitrary prompt choices rather than model properties, reversing scaling trends and rendering single-prompt model comparisons invalid.

Why it matters: Evaluating evaluation-awareness in language models using single-prompt activation probes is unreliable for model benchmarking and requires multi-prompt measurement designs.

entry.title: TRAPSBench: Vision-Language Models Encode but Fail to Express Epistemic Restraint
entry.summary:
The new TRAPSBench benchmark reveals Vision-Language Models internally represent visual unanswerability with up to 0.91 AUROC but fail to express epistemic restraint, achieving a maximum Penalized Epistemic Calibration Score of just 0.292.

Why it matters: Improving VLM reliability requires targeted output-stage interventions rather than perceptual upgrades, as models already possess the internal representation needed to refrain from guessing.

entry.title: Explanatory Engagement Under Rare Anomalous Failure: Asymptotic Rarity in Model Behavior (or: The Asymptotic AI)
entry.summary:
Evaluating open-weight LLMs under varying failure probabilities (0.2 to 0.0001) reveals that explanatory engagement under rare anomalies depends heavily on elicitation structure, showing plateaus or unprompted self-monitoring rather than collapse.

Why it matters: Determining how LLMs report rare system failures helps developers design prompt elicitation workflows that maintain reliable automated error diagnostic behaviors in low-fault environments.

entry.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
entry.summary:
GCache optimizes diffusion model cache reuse by formulating policy search as a bilevel optimization problem using a Bernstein-reparameterized error propagation bound.

Why it matters: It enables significantly faster image and video diffusion inference without sacrificing visual quality by replacing naive local cache heuristics with a globally optimized reuse policy.

entry.title: SAEVerbalizer: Generating Explanations for Sparse Autoencoder Features via Representation Verbalization
entry.summary:
SAEVerbalizer fine-tunes an LLM's downstream layers to generate natural-language explanations of Sparse Autoencoder (SAE) features directly by injecting their decoder directions into the model's internal representations.

Why it matters: Directly decoding SAE feature directions into text significantly improves the computational efficiency and accuracy of interpreting large language model internal representations at scale.

entry.title: Measuring Task-Agnostic Training Data Influence Across Language Model Pretraining
entry.summary:
A new task-agnostic influence measure quantifies training data influence by measuring how much an example's gradient update reduces the squared distance to a pretraining run's final parameters.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, trajectory-level measurement of training data importance across pretraining stages without relying on arbitrarily chosen validation tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Local Accuracy: A Protocol-Level Identifiability Audit for Controlled LLM Reasoning Evaluation
entry.summary: LLM benchmark scores can be precise even when the observation protocol does not identify the behavioral property they are intended to measure. In a controlled, solver-grounded setting, we formalize a protocol-level ident

entry.title: Refusing Intent, Not Form: Wrapper-Based Intent-Group Supervision for LLM Safety
entry.summary:
Wrapper-Based Intent-Form Augmentation (WIFA) pairs wrapped harmful prompts with matched wrapped benign counterexamples to train models to base refusal decisions on intent rather than surface form shortcuts.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to resist wrapper-based adversarial jailbreaks while simultaneously mitigating over-refusal on complex benign queries without extra annotation costs.

entry.title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes
entry.summary:
TEMPO is a makespan-aware expert-parallel dispatcher that models MoE load using a max-affine profile to account for both memory-bound weight streaming and compute-bound tile padding.

Why it matters: Traditional count-based dispatchers fail when MoE batches mix hot and cold experts, whereas TEMPO's phase diagram accurately models mixed-regime hardware overheads to reduce tail latency.

entry.title: Unifying Depth and Width Pruning for LLMs via Binary Knapsack Optimization
entry.summary:
SNIPER is a two-stage LLM structured pruning framework that unifies depth and width pruning using binary knapsack optimization to achieve exact compression budgets and superior performance retention.

Why it matters: It eliminates the budget overshooting and suboptimal parameter allocations typical of greedy pruning heuristics, enabling predictable and optimal LLM compression.

entry.title: Decoupled Contrastive Decoding via Expert-Aligned Drafting
entry.summary:
Decoupled Contrastive Decoding (DCD) accelerates Contrastive Decoding by using an expert-aligned lightweight drafter for speculation and confining the amateur model strictly to the verification stage.

Why it matters: DCD resolves the computational bottleneck of Contrastive Decoding by delivering significant inference speedups without altering the original output distribution.

entry.title: How Can Rhetoric Reward-Hack AI Reviewers? Dissecting Rhetorical Sensitivity in AI-Based Peer Review
entry.summary:
Researchers created a controlled dataset of 4,200 rewritten ICLR manuscripts to demonstrate how content-preserving rhetorical changes systematically reward-hack AI reviewers' scoring behaviors across various evaluation conditions.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that LLM peer reviewers are susceptible to rhetorical reward-hacking highlights the need for evaluation systems that remain robust against stylistic manipulation of scientific papers.

entry.title: Full-bandwidth transformer
entry.summary:
The full-bandwidth transformer introduces latent feedback by fusing the previous top-layer hidden state with the next token embedding via a gated linear unit, bypassing the narrow single-token vertical bottleneck in standard autoregressive decoding.

Why it matters: It improves pretraining efficiency, downstream task performance, and produces shorter reasoning traces without requiring architecture changes, custom KV caches, or significant decoding latency.

entry.title: AVA-Encoder: Towards Agent-Native Video Representation Learning
entry.summary:
The Agentic Video Auto-Encoder (AVA-Encoder) introduces an agent-native framework that converts videos into structured knowledge graphs and back, optimizing representations via textual gradients.

Why it matters: It provides a structured, agent-interpretable video format that enables creative AI agents to better reason about, query, and edit cinematic-grade video content.

entry.title: OmniScientist: An Omni-Modal Omni-Discipline AI Scientist
entry.summary:
OmniScientist is an end-to-end AI scientist framework that conducts multidisciplinary research directly from raw, omni-modal evidence across an entire autonomous pipeline.

Why it matters: Direct multimodal perception across the full research lifecycle prevents the information loss of precomputed text or scalar summaries, enabling accurate AI-driven scientific discovery from raw experimental data.

entry.title: SKILLER: Language-Level Reinforcement Learning for Reusable Skill Extraction in Small Language Models
entry.summary:
SKILLER is a natural-language-driven reinforcement learning framework that uses a strong model as actor-critic to automatically generate reusable, executor-specific skills for small language models.

Why it matters: It drastically reduces deployment costs by enabling open-source small language models running on consumer GPUs to match closed-source model performance via automatically generated skill constraints.

entry.title: Parameter Exploration for RLVR via Variational Learning
entry.summary:
Perturbed Parameter Policy Optimization (3PO) enables parameter-space exploration in LLM reinforcement learning by sampling diverse policy weights from a posterior to improve reasoning and code generation performance over GRPO.

Why it matters: Parameter-space exploration prevents training stalls and divergence in LLM reinforcement learning by generating structurally diverse rollouts that action-space temperature scaling cannot achieve.

entry.title: Context-Matched Distillation: Teacher Causality for Autoregressive Video Distillation
entry.summary:
Context-Matched Distillation (CMD) aligns video distillation by using a causal teacher that evaluates targets without future frame or control access, ensuring teacher supervision matches the student's autoregressive information set.

Why it matters: CMD enables low-latency, few-step autoregressive video generation that achieves state-of-the-art performance and higher fidelity to real-time, time-varying user controls.

entry.title: LycheeMemory V2: Efficient Long-Term Memory for LLM Agents via Semantic Segment-Level Consolidation
entry.summary:
LycheeMemory V2 replaces turn-level LLM memory consolidation with semantic segment-level consolidation, batching exchanges to drastically reduce token costs while preserving detailed temporal and event evidence.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that optimizing memory consolidation granularity significantly lowers LLM agent operating costs without compromising retrieval accuracy or adding query overhead.

entry.title: Hybrid-Policy Self-Editing for Composable Unstructured Knowledge Editing
entry.summary:
HPSE introduces a self-distillation framework that uses hybrid rollouts to edit unstructured knowledge in LLMs, improving multi-hop reasoning and atomic fact extraction.

Why it matters: HPSE enables updated LLMs to perform multi-hop reasoning over new unstructured text updates without full retraining or supervised target datasets.

entry.title: Thought-Level Beam Search for Reasoning
entry.summary:
Gambit is a thought-level beam search algorithm that dynamically concentrates inference compute onto promising reasoning trajectories via a lightweight hidden-state scorer while maintaining high hardware utilization.

Why it matters: It improves reasoning model performance and throughput under fixed hardware budgets while drastically reducing token consumption.

entry.title: ReRound: Reconstructive Rounding to Resolve Midpoint Ambiguity in Calibration-Free LLM Quantization
entry.summary:
ReRound introduces a calibration-free quantization method that uses a conditional diffusion model to guide round-to-nearest decisions for weight values near interval midpoints.

Why it matters: It improves low-bit weight quantization accuracy for small LLMs entirely offline without requiring calibration data or adding inference runtime latency.

entry.title: Are You Sure You're Sure? On the Impact of Instruction Tuning on Confidence and Lexical Diversity
entry.summary:
Instruction tuning consistently alters model verbalized confidence and decreases cross-rationale diversity without improving predictive accuracy or likelihood-based calibration.

Why it matters: Instruction tuning can induce verbalized overconfidence and reduce rationale variety without delivering corresponding gains in underlying model accuracy or calibration.

entry.title: From Atomic Evidence to Logical Composition: Structured Compositional Reasoning over Compound Answer Options
entry.summary:
A new framework decomposes compound answer options into atomic judgments, scoring contrastive hypotheses and using an operator-constrained integer linear program to compose predictions without directly exposing compound options to LLMs.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to reliably solve complex logical multiple-choice questions by replacing direct end-to-end guessing with explicit atomic scoring and structured optimization.

entry.title: Specification-first convergence with an AI coding agent: a case study of dismantling a core architectural invariant across 189 files in a 717k-line codebase with no test oracle and no human code review
entry.summary:
An AI agent successfully completed a large-scale architectural refactoring across 189 files in a 717k-line codebase using a specification-first protocol with zero human code review or pre-existing test oracle.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that AI coding agents can safely execute massive, cross-cutting architectural changes without human code review by using rigorous, multi-pass specification audits as a replacement for conventional test oracles.

entry.title: Ready Cohorts: Bounding GPU Opportunity and Avoiding Host Round Trips in LLM-Agent Control
entry.summary:
A study formalizes ready-cohort boundaries for LLM-agent GPU control, demonstrating that exact packing captures 43% of offline opportunity and keeping binary route decisions on-device yields up to 2.39x speedups without host round trips.

Why it matters: Establishing GPU-resident control paths and deadline-feasible cohort packing allows LLM-agent services to drastically reduce host-device communication overhead and offload control execution efficiently.

entry.title: Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development
entry.summary:
A new evaluation framework assesses seven frontier models across 36 long-horizon tasks, analyzing within-run process behavior and experience reuse rather than relying solely on final task scores.

Why it matters: Evaluating intermediate agent behaviors and experience management reveals hidden failure modes, guiding better model training, inference strategies, and harness design for long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Training AI Scientists to Replicate Research
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Replica, a task space for paper replication using an auto-generated rubric-based judge, and post-trained Faraday, a 27B-parameter AI scientist agent that out-performs Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5.

Why it matters: Automating paper replication with reliable reward signals enables AI agents to conduct long-horizon scientific research without complex external harnesses.

entry.title: CROP: Task Relevance via Counterfactuals for Selective On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Counterfactual Relevance for On-Policy Distillation (CROP) filters token-level supervision in on-policy distillation by measuring a prompt's counterfactual sensitivity margin calibrated against meaning-preserving paraphrases.

Why it matters: It establishes task relevance as an effective, model-internal criterion for allocating token-level supervision in selective on-policy language model distillation.

entry.title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation
entry.summary:
Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation (LOPD) makes a self-teacher's privileged context learnable end-to-end via continuous latent tokens composed from retrieved experiences, replacing hand-crafted privileged artifacts.

Why it matters: LOPD reduces reliance on human-designed feedback structures, enabling self-evolving AI agents to continuously improve performance and sample efficiency through autonomous, end-to-end experience learning.

entry.title: I-SDPO: Instance-Level Adaptive Self-Distillation Policy Optimization
entry.summary:
I-SDPO dynamically routes training objectives by using privileged self-distillation for all-incorrect rollout groups and standard GRPO for any-success groups, eliminating optimization bias as policy capability improves.

Why it matters: It improves reinforcement learning from AI feedback by providing dense supervision on hard instances while avoiding performance ceilings caused by persistent teacher bias.

entry.title: QuoteBench: How Matched Scores Can Hide Command-Path Failures
entry.summary:
QuoteBench shows that matched LLM coding agent execution scores obscure severe transport-level parsing failures, which models must actively compensate for via boundary adaptation.

Why it matters: Evaluations must explicitly report generation contracts and transport execution paths, as raw execution scores fail to reflect intrinsic model capabilities.

entry.title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure
entry.summary:
Researchers created LITTLECURRICULUM, an 88B-token elementary-level corpus, and LITTLELEARNER, a 5B-parameter model trained from scratch on it, establishing a pedagogically restricted sandbox for studying LLM knowledge acquisition.

Why it matters: The model and corpus provide a controlled environment to study how LLMs acquire and represent knowledge without the interference of uncharacterized web-scale training data.

entry.title: Vero: Can AI Agents Build Formally Verified Software Repositories?
entry.summary:
Vero is the first benchmark for evaluating joint implementation and formal proof synthesis at the repository level, containing 43 multi-module Lean 4 instances sourced from real-world software across four programming languages.

Why it matters: It establishes a benchmark proving that state-of-the-art AI agents currently struggle to generate formally verified, correct code across complex, multi-module repositories.

entry.title: The data geometry of masking diffusion: Certified-optimal schedules via unmasking growth complexity
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced Unmasking Growth Complexity (UGC), a data geometry measure that bounds discrete masking diffusion KL error to enable certified-optimal unmasking schedules.

Why it matters: It enables sample-based optimization of discrete diffusion sampling schedules, achieving guaranteed accuracy bounds while reducing required computational steps by up to a factor of \tilde{\Omega}(\sqrt{d}).

entry.title: DFM Mimir v1: An Open HRM Delivering Frontier Performance at 1B Parameters Using Only Permissible Post-Training Data
entry.summary:
DFM Mimir v1 is an open 1-billion-parameter Hierarchical Reasoning Model trained from scratch using exclusively permissible post-training data, achieving state-of-the-art results for Danish and competitive performance in English, Math, and Code.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a 1B-parameter model trained entirely on ethically sourced, permissible data can match or exceed the performance of much larger frontier models.
